record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: Should superconductivity be excluded in manganites, or can a doped or pressure-tuned manganite near a metal-insulator or quantum-critical regime support superconductivity; and if superconductivity still never appears, does that imply the spin-1/2 character of cuprates is essential in a way that higher-spin manganites are not?

evidence.quote: Should we totally exclude superconductivity as a possibility in manganites? ... Is there a doped-manganite compound, likely a large bandwidth one, that does not order at low temperatures and maintains a metallic character? Or, alternatively, can a metallic manganite compound become paramagnetic upon the application of, e.g., high pressure, at low temperatures?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of perovskite manganite compounds of the form R₁₋ₓAₓMnO₃, where R is a trivalent rare-earth ion (e.g., La, Pr, Nd, Sm) and A is a divalent alkaline-earth ion (e.g., Ca, Sr, Ba). These materials exhibit a rich phase diagram including ferromagnetic metallic, antiferromagnetic insulating, charge-ordered, and orbital-ordered phases, and colossal magnetoresistance near magnetic-ordering transitions. The Mn ions carry spins S ≥ 1 (e.g., S = 3/2 for Mn⁴⁺ and S = 2 for Mn³⁺), in contrast with the spin-1/2 Cu²⁺ ions of the cuprate superconductors.

Address the following questions:

(a) Does there exist a choice of cations R, A and a hole-doping fraction x (preferably in a large-bandwidth manganite family) such that the resulting compound remains metallic and paramagnetic down to arbitrarily low temperatures, without ordering into any magnetic, charge-ordered, or orbital-ordered phase?

(b) Alternatively, can such a metallic, non-ordering low-temperature state be reached in some manganite by tuning a non-thermal control parameter (for example, hydrostatic pressure or chemical substitution) toward a metal–insulator transition or a magnetic quantum critical point?

(c) In any such regime, can a bulk superconducting phase emerge in a manganite at low temperatures, or must superconductivity be rigorously excluded from the manganite phase diagram on general grounds?

(d) If the conclusion of (c) is that no manganite supports bulk superconductivity, determine whether this absence necessarily implies that the spin-1/2 nature of the magnetic ions in the cuprates plays an essential role in the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity that cannot be replicated by higher-spin (S > 1/2) transition-metal oxides.
artifact.category_tag: Strongly correlated electron systems / manganite superconductivity
artifact.status_search_result: No established bulk superconducting manganite has been reported. Some studies report fragmentary or filamentary signatures of superconductivity in frustrated manganites such as La₁₋ySmyMnO₃₊δ at low temperatures, but these are not confirmed as bulk superconductivity. Whether a paramagnetic-metallic manganite near a quantum-critical or metal–insulator regime can host superconductivity, and the implied role of spin-1/2 character in cuprates, remain open.

status_evidence.title: Signs of high-temperature superconductivity in frustrated manganites La1−ySmyMnO3+δ
status_evidence.snippet: Signs of high-temperature superconductivity have been revealed for the first time in frustrated manganites... a small fraction of the superconducting phase coexisting with charge and antiferromagnetic correlations.
status_evidence.claim: Only fractional/filamentary superconducting signatures have been reported in manganites; bulk superconductivity has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Mixed-valence manganites (Coey, Viret, von Molnár)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive review of mixed-valence manganite phase diagrams with no bulk superconducting phase reported.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reviews of manganites do not include a bulk superconducting phase.
